Under Rule 10 of the DPDP Rules 2025, the fiduciary must check, before creating a child's account, that the parent is an identifiable adult. It does this by checking reliable identity and age details the fiduciary already holds for a registered parent (Case 1), or by checking identity and age details issued by a body entrusted by law or the Government, or a virtual token mapped to them, with the parent optionally using a Digital Locker service provider (Case 2).

Sources: DPDP Rules 2025, Rule 10 (parts 1–3, pp. 27–28). I could not retrieve the full text of Case 3 and Case 4 (the chunk for part 3 was refused on a repeat call, so I used the search excerpt), and the RBI NBFC KYC Directions were not relevant to this question.

content.text: The corpus does not contain a direct prohibition on child-directed tracking or targeted advertising, and nothing addresses app or card usage data. The DPDP Rules' Fourth Schedule restricts tracking and behavioural monitoring of children to listed purposes (educational institutions, crèches, transport, child safety), and Part B item 5 requires that any advertisement likely to cause a detrimental effect on a child's well-being be kept from her. The Act's general prohibition on such processing (section 9(3)) did not come up in my searches, so I could not quote it, and the RBI NBFC Directions I searched did not surface any child-specific rule on app or card usage data.

Yes. Rule 10 of the DPDP Rules 2025 requires a Data Fiduciary to obtain verifiable parental consent before processing any personal data of a child, and the rule sets no exception for teenagers aged 13 to 17. The rule defines "adult" as someone who has completed 18 years, so a 13- to 17-year-old cannot give that consent alone, and the corpus contains no provision letting a teen sign up without parental involvement. I did not retrieve the Act's own definition of "child" (which I understand to be under 18), so that point rests on the rule's adult definition rather than a direct quote.

findings.obligation: A Data Fiduciary must adopt technical and organisational measures to obtain verifiable parental consent before processing any personal data of a child (under 18). A 13-17 year old cannot validly consent alone.
findings.recommendation: Redesign onboarding so a parent or guardian is identified and gives verifiable consent before any child data (name, date of birth, phone number) is processed. Do not allow self sign-up without this step.

findings.obligation: The Data Fiduciary must check that the person claiming to be the parent is an identifiable adult. It does this using reliable identity and age details it already holds, or details voluntarily provided by the parent, including through a government-authorised entity's virtual token or a Digital Locker service provider.
findings.recommendation: Build a parent verification flow. For existing users, confirm the data held is reliable. For new parents, verify age and identity through government-issued details, a virtual token or DigiLocker before creating the child's account.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: When an NBFC establishes an account-based relationship, it must carry out CDD by obtaining Aadhaar or an OVD (or equivalent e-document, or KYC Identifier) and PAN or Form 60, and must verify these. Self-declared name, date of birth and phone number do not meet this. Minor-specific or guardian provisions are not stated in the passages given.
findings.recommendation: Confirm with compliance how KYC applies to minors and the guardian's role. Do not onboard minors on self-declared details alone. Obtain and verify the required identity documents, involving the guardian where the Directions require it.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: Verification must follow prescribed methods: offline verification of Aadhaar, digital signature verification of e-documents with a live photo, digital KYC, or CKYCR retrieval. A simplified procedure applies only where the person cannot produce the documents, and only under stated conditions.
findings.recommendation: Add an identity verification step (Aadhaar offline verification, OVD e-document, Digital KYC or V-CIP). Use the simplified procedure only if its conditions are met and documented.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: Accounts opened non-face-to-face (a remote app sign-up) are subject to enhanced due diligence. Such customers are categorised as high-risk, and the first transaction must be a credit from the customer's existing KYC-compliant bank account.
findings.recommendation: Apply EDD controls to remote onboarding. Fund the first transaction from an existing KYC-compliant account, and treat these accounts as high-risk with enhanced monitoring.

findings.obligation: The child-data protections in section 9 (parental consent, no tracking or behavioural monitoring) are relaxed only for the listed purposes, such as real-time location for safety, or preventing access to harmful content. A pocket-money app's usage tracking or ad targeting is not among them.
findings.recommendation: Do not track, behaviourally monitor or target advertising at child users. Limit any processing to what the Fourth Schedule exemptions allow, and document the basis.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: If the card has any credit component, the NBFC must assess creditworthiness, including age, occupation and income, before extending a loan. It must also provide a Key Facts Statement with APR and all charges to the borrower. Credit card receivables are exempt from the KFS rules. The passages do not address capacity of minors.
findings.recommendation: Keep the product strictly prepaid or debit-like with no credit or overdraft for under-18s. If any credit or fee element is planned, obtain legal advice on contractual capacity, run the age, occupation and income assessment, and provide a KFS and clear charge disclosure.

(c) “Digital Locker service provider” shall mean such intermediary, including a body corporate or an
agency of the appropriate Government, as may be notified by the Central Government, in
accordance with the rules made in this regard under the Information Technology Act, 2000 (21 of
2000);
Illustration.
C is a child, P is a parent, and DF is a Data Fiduciary. A user account of C is sought to be created
on the online platform of DF, by processing the personal data of C.
Case 1: C informs DF that she is a child and declares P as her parent. DF shall enable P to identify
herself through its website, app or other appropriate means. P identifies herself as the parent and informs
DF that she is a registered user on DF’s platform and has previously made available her identity and age
details to DF. Before processing C’s personal data for the creation of her user account, DF shall check to
confirm that it holds reliable identity and age details of P and that P is an identifiable adult.
Case 2: C informs DF that she is a child and declares P as her parent. DF shall enable P to identify
herself through its website, app or other appropriate means. P identifies herself as the parent and informs
DF that she herself is not a registered user on DF’s platform. Before processing C’s personal data for the
creation of her user account, DF shall, by reference to identity and age details issued by an entity entrusted
by law or the Government with maintenance of the said details or to a virtual token mapped to the identity
and age, check that P is an identifiable adult. P may voluntarily make such details available using the
services of a Digital Locker service provider.
Case 3: P is opening an account for C and identifies herself as C’s parent and informs DF that she
is a registered user on DF’s platform and has previously made available her identity and age details to DF.

term loans sanctioned on or after October 1, 2024, including fresh loans to existing
customers, by an NBFC. Credit card receivables are exempted from the provisions
given below:
(1) An NBFC shall provide a KFS to all prospective borrowers to help them take an
informed view before executing the loan contract, as per the standardised format

borrowers. Contents of KFS shall be explained to the borrower and an
acknowledgement shall be obtained that they have understood the same.

validity period of at least three working days for loans having tenor of seven days
or more, and a validity period of one working day for loans having tenor of less than
seven days.

provided the KFS by the NBFC, to agree to the terms of the loan. The NBFC shall

during the validity period.

23. For undertaking CDD, the NBFC shall obtain the following from an individual
while establishing an account-based relationship or while dealing with the individual
who is a beneficial owner, authorised signatory or the power of attorney holder related
to any legal entity:
(1) the Aadhaar number where,
(i) they are desirous of receiving any benefit or subsidy under any scheme notified
under section 7 of the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other subsidies,
Benefits and Services) Act, 2016 (18 of 2016); or
(ii) they decide to submit their Aadhaar number voluntarily to a NBFC or any RE
notified under the first proviso to sub-section (1) of section 11A of the PML Act; or
(2) the proof of possession of Aadhaar number where the NBFC can carry out
offline verification; or
(3) the proof of possession of Aadhaar number where the NBFC cannot carry out
the offline verification or any OVD or the equivalent e-document thereof containing the
details of their identity and address; or
(4) the KYC Identifier with an explicit consent to download records from CKYCR;
and
(5) the PAN or the equivalent e-document thereof or Form No. 60 as defined in
Income-tax Rules, 1962; and
(6) the NBFC may require such other documents including in respect of the nature
of business and financial status of the customer, or the equivalent e-documents
thereof.
Provided that where the customer has submitted,
(i) Aadhaar number under clause (1) above to a NBFC notified under first proviso
to sub-section (1) of section 11A of the PML Act, such NBFC shall carry out
authentication of the customer’s Aadhaar number using UIDAI’s e-KYC authentication.
Further, in such a case, if the customer wants to provide a current address, different
from the address as per the identity information available in the Central Identities Data
Repository, they may give a self-declaration to that effect to the NBFC.
